title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
items.abstract: <jats:p>Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. BPE's pretokenizer splits on whitespace before merges are learned, so no multi-word string can ever become a single token: in Qwen3-4B, "United States of America" is four tokens and no adjacent pair of them exists as one entry, so a phrase is out of reach of any method drafting in the target's vocabulary. We change the unit. A small MLP head reads the frozen target's hidden state and predicts a one- to three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary; greedy longest-match expansion maps it back into the target's own tokens, and N candidates are verified in one forward pass behind a prefix-tree mask, so the change is orthogonal to tree depth and width. The target and its tokenizer stay frozen and a candidate is accepted only while it matches the target's own argmax, so the served output is identical to greedy decoding up to floating-point tie-breaking. On one A5000 at batch 1, against HuggingFace generate(), a 21.94M head (0.545% of Qwen3-4B) reaches 2.391x on GSM8K, 2.444x on MATH-500 and 1.544x on MT-Bench. Because the head's output layer is one row of 257 parameters per entry, the draft vocabulary size is the parameter budget: an 8,000-entry head is 3.434M parameters, 0.0854% of the target and 64x smaller than EAGLE-3's drafter, and keeps 92.3% of the larger head's GSM8K tokens per pass. With EAGLE-3 run on same prompts and baseline, our 21.94M head is ahead of tree-16 on both maths sets and behind tree-60 on every set.</jats:p>

title: Transactional KV Caching for Speculative Decoding under Paged KV Memory
items.abstract: <jats:p>Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by verifying multiple draft tokens per targetmodel forward pass while preserving the target distribution [3, 8]. In parallel, modern serving engines rely on paged KV-cache memory (e.g., Page-dAttention/vLLM) to minimize fragmentation and support prefix sharing across requests [7, 16]. However, speculative decoding induces temporary KV growth for uncommitted draft tokens, which interacts poorly with block-granular KV allocation and token-budget schedulers. Production documentation explicitly notes that draft tokens consume extra KV-cache pages and count toward global token limits, limiting observed speedups at higher load [12, 14]. We propose TransKV, a transactional KV-cache abstraction that separates stable committed KV state from a packed speculative KV buffer. Speculative KV writes remain uncommitted until acceptance is known; only the accepted prefix is committed into the paged cache and rejected KV is discarded without rollback. We provide a formal memory and scheduling analysis showing speculative KV pressure reduces from block-sized pages to token-sized buffers. This reduction yields significant concurrency improvements in capacity-limited prefix-shared branching workloads (e.g., up to 1.78× at 𝐵=16, 𝑚=2). On real GPUs (Kaggle Tesla P100 16 GiB and Colab Tesla T4 15 GiB), TransKV increases achievable branch concurrency by up to 1.78× at 𝐵=16, 𝑚=2 and by 1.60× at 𝐵=16, 𝑚=4, with exact output equivalence by construction.</jats:p>
items.publisher: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)

title: Multi-Tenant Edge-Cloud Hybrid LLM Serving using Speculative Decoding and Quantization
items.abstract: The inference of large language models faces a fundamental dilemma between edge inference, which preserves privacy but is hardware-constrained, and cloud inference, which suffers from network latency and inefficient resource utilization. In this paper, we propose a multi-tenant hybrid inference architecture that leverages collaborative speculative decoding to mitigate these trade-offs. We employ a W4A16-quantized edge draft model to maintain high speculative accuracy while reducing memory footprints, paired with an asynchronous communication protocol to mask wide-area network latency. To address cloud-side resource idleness, we introduce a multi-tenant verification orchestrator, which multiplexes concurrent verification requests from heterogeneous edge devices to maximize GPU throughput. Our analytical model demonstrates that this framework effectively decouples edge execution from cloud handshake loops and eliminates the mutual waiting bottleneck. Theoretical analysis indicates that the proposed system scales efficiently under multi-tenant workloads, providing a scalable and privacy-preserving path for edge-cloud collaborative LLM deployment.
